issues.problem: 胡适原话是“至少获得了部分的胜利”，这是一个保底式的肯定。稿件中文用“但他称之为‘部分的胜利’”构成转折，英文写成“Yet he called it only a partial victory”，把“至少”改成了“只”，方向与原文相反，削弱了胡适自己的评价。

evidence.quote: 因此在我们的斗争中，至少获得了部分的胜利。其中重要的部分就是以白话文为教育的工具。

issues.proposed: 中文改为：他说这场斗争“至少获得了部分的胜利”，其中重要的部分是以白话为教育工具。英文改为：He said the struggle had won at least a partial victory, the important part being the vernacular as the instrument of education. 同时删去“Yet”“only”及中文的“但”。
issues.rationale: 胡适原话“至少获得了部分的胜利”是保底式肯定。原稿中文的“但他称之为”构成转折，英文的“Yet … only a partial victory”把“至少”译成了“只”，方向与原文相反。现在删去“但”“Yet”“only”。中文改为直接转述其原话“至少获得了部分的胜利”，英文相应改为 at least a partial victory，中英一致。其余句子未改动。

edits.before: This piece rests on a single source: Hu Shi's oral memoir in later life, itself abridged, revised in his own hand and translated back. Mei Guangdi's and Ren Hongjun's words and deeds reach us only through Hu's retelling; Hu's explanations of motive are retrospective; and Tang Degang's notes are commentary rather than fact. Paragraphs marked interpretation are the author's inferences, paragraphs marked modern are scenarios invented for readers today; neither is drawn from the material this piece relies on.

edits.before: Hu's own explanation of how it all happened is that he opposed single-cause theories of history. He used to joke that accidents matter more than any monistic cause — economics, lust, God and the rest: those single causes explain everything that has ever happened, and precisely because they explain everything, they explain nothing. In this episode he explicitly called the farewell poem a small accident, and said that a chain of small accidents had gradually forced him into his position; placing the leaflet and the dispute that followed the near-capsize on the lake in that chain is this article's own grouping. Reading a chain of small accidents as the push behind his position is Hu's own view of history, not a finding of this article.

edits.before: After the note was sent, he regretted it. Zhong was a kind man with a sincere wish to reform Chinese customs and writing; the rudeness was uncalled for, and Hu reproached himself before his friends. Then a further thought: if men like Zhong are not qualified to discuss such questions, then the qualified should do the work — set out what is feasible and what is not, and examine both. He took it up with Zhao Yuanren, who had entered Cornell with him in 1910. They agreed to make "the question of China's writing" the literature section's topic for the annual meeting of the Chinese Students' Association in the East, and split it: Zhao on whether the Chinese script could adopt an alphabetic system and how to proceed; Hu on "how to make our classical written language easier to teach."

edits.before: Hu's paper called the classical written language a "half-dead language." Some words live, some have died: gou, "dog," is still in use; quan, the old word for the same animal, is not. "Ride a horse" is everyday speech; the classical equivalent is a dead phrase. So the teaching of a living language and of a half-dead one must be very different business. Looking back, he said his doctrine — vernacular alive, classical half-dead — had begun in this period.

edits.before: It appeared in New Youth in January 1917 and stirred a great response. Two Peking University professors took it seriously. Chen Duxiu, an unbending revolutionary, answered with "On Literary Revolution," publicly backing a literary revolution and saying frankly that the banner had been raised by his friend Hu Shi; he himself was raising the banner high in his friend's support. Qian Xuantong, professor of classical phonology, a master of ancient prose and a disciple of the great scholar Zhang Taiyan, wrote no article but sent Chen and Hu long letters — small criticisms, great praise — also printed in New Youth; that so eminent a classicist should sympathize buoyed their cause. Zhao Yuanren often said that Hu's vernacular poems and essays were "not vernacular enough," not the genuine spoken style ordinary people used. Hu admitted it: like a woman who had bound her feet for forty, or even twenty, years, however much she loosened the bindings she would never recover natural feet.

edits.before: 结局也可以交代一笔。胡适自述，运动约四年就在学校教育上基本成功：1920年北京政府教育部通令，国民小学一、二年级教材一律改用白话，旧教材分期废除。但他称之为“部分的胜利”，重要的部分是以白话为教育工具；他同时说，1919年的学生运动把文化运动变成了政治运动，对文艺复兴运动是一种“干扰”，虽则对传播白话文功不可没。

edits.before: The outcome can be set down too. By Hu's account, in only about four years the effort to replace the classical language with the vernacular in the schools had all but succeeded: in 1920 the Ministry of Education of the Beijing government ordered that all first- and second-year textbooks in the national primary schools be written entirely in the vernacular, with the old textbooks abolished in stages. Yet he called it only a partial victory; the important part was making the vernacular the instrument of education. He also said the student movement of 1919 had been an interruption to the Renaissance movement, turning a cultural movement into a political one, though it did much to spread the vernacular.

issues.proposed: 中文改为“凡文中写明‘作者推断’‘一种解释’的段落是作者推断，‘设想’‘虚构场景’部分是为今日读者虚构的场景”；英文同步改为“Passages flagged as the author's inference or a possible reading are inferences, and the scenarios introduced as hypothetical are invented for readers today.”

verify.overall: 定稿的事实、引语、时序、归属与中英对应均有证据支持；推断已标明，现代场景未冒充记录，开头易读性合格；仅有三处易读性小问题，建议顺手修改。

issues.problem: 末句“并非本文所据材料的记载 / not something recorded in the material this piece relies on”是在断言完整来源没写什么。本文只依据证据包，无法替全书作此断言。而且证据确实记载了陈独秀本人表述的分工：胡适首举义旗，陈高张大旗声援。这样写会误导读者，以为来源对此毫无记载。真正属于推断的只是“刻意配合”这一层，应标为本文的推断。

evidence.quote: 他自己则高张大旗为他的朋友作声援

issues.proposed: 中文改为“……的配合，是作者从先后次序读出的一种可能，属本文的推断。”英文改为“…is a possibility the author reads in the sequence — this article's inference.”

issues.problem: 末半句“都不是本文所据材料的记述 / neither is drawn from the material this piece relies on”属于来源未载类断言。前文已分别标明这些段落是作者推断、虚构场景，这半句对读者理解没有必要。
issues.proposed: 删去中文“，都不是本文所据材料的记述”和英文“; neither is drawn from the material this piece relies on”，保留“是作者推断”“是为今日读者虚构的场景”。

issues.problem: 英文“accidents matter more than any monistic cause”漏掉了限定词“往往”，把胡适“往往更重要”的说法写成了绝对判断。中文保留了“往往”，中英不一致。
